subject: Emergency slate carve-in & short-notice autoscale exception for Atlas.ai pilot
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mike Chen <mike@atlasai.com>
Date: Mon, Jul 19, 2026 at 08:12 AM -0700
Subject: Emergency slate carve-in & short-notice autoscale exception for Atlas.ai pilot

Team —

Heads-up: Atlas.ai just confirmed they want to run a high-fidelity pilot next week (3-day window) that will spike us above normal pilot headroom. They asked for a short-notice carve-in of dedicated GPUs and an autoscale policy exception to allow burst beyond our usual cap for the duration.

High-level ask:
- Carve-in: 10 x A100-equivalent GPUs from the US dedicated pool, 72-hour window starting 2026-07-22 09:00 PT
- Autoscale exception: allow temporary burst to 16 concurrent slots for that pool (normally capped at 8 for pilots)
- Ops runbook: a lightweight mitigation playbook and rollback criteria that we can hand to on-call

Attached: atlas-poc-load-profile.csv (expected QPS/token profile), proposed-mop.txt (initial ops asks).

Why now: Atlas is a strategic partner and this pilot is on the critical path for a marketplace channel integration. They will sign a simple MOU and cover incremental GPU hours. Their expected peak looks aggressive (see CSV) but they can shift load-window by a few hours if that helps.

Immediate questions for you:
1) Marcus — kernel/compat and model pinning: do we have technical blockers to a short carve-in?
2) Kimberly/Laura — policy and prioritization: can we grant this without impacting committed Dedicated SLAs for other customers? If not, what partial carve looks acceptable?
3) Dev/Soojin — ops & autoscale: what approvals do we need and how fast can we produce a runbook?

I know this is short notice. I recommend we triage availability and propose a conservative fallback (e.g., standby lane of 4 GPUs + a conditional autoscale to 10) if full 10/16 is not feasible.

Can we sync in 2 hours?

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: atlas-poc-load-profile.csv (CSV), proposed-mop.txt (text)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mike Chen <mike@atlasai.com>
Date: Mon, Jul 19, 2026 at 09:50 AM -0700
Subject: Re: Emergency slate carve-in & short-notice autoscale exception for Atlas.ai pilot

Irene —

Thanks for the context. Quick summary from policy/eng side after scanning the load profile:
- Committed Dedicated SLAs: we cannot evict paying customers on short notice; any carve must come from transient/burst capacity or pre-approved standby lanes.
- Current headroom: US pool has ~6 GPUs in burstable capacity today and a reserved standby lane of 4 that we can allocate for a short window without SLA impact.
- Risk: if we push beyond burstable capacity to pull GPUs from warm reserved pools, we will need executive approval and potentially credits for affected customers.

Proposal (fast path):
1) Offer standby lane of 4 GPUs immediately for the 72-hour window.
2) In parallel, attempt to free up +4 GPUs by moving noncritical eval jobs to preemptible nodes for that 72-hour window (requires Marcus + Dev to confirm).
3) Autoscale exception: allow conditional burst to 10 concurrent slots if the freed GPUs are validated — this is an ops-gated exception (on-call signoff required).

If Atlas insists on 10 guaranteed GPUs, we need to open an escalation with Sales Ops and Legal to confirm credits and customer communication.

Quick clarifying Qs for Atlas (Mike, cc'd):
- Can you shift the start window by +/- 12 hours if that gives us more runway?
- Please confirm the absolute minimum guaranteed GPUs you need vs. peak burst tolerances.

Irene, Marcus — I can join the sync in 2 hours.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Dedicated Capacity Programs
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, Jul 19, 2026 at 11:08 AM -0700
Subject: Re: Emergency slate carve-in & short-notice autoscale exception for Atlas.ai pilot

Folks —

Technical check-list after looking at their load CSV and asking infra team:
- Model variant: Atlas told us they're running a 70B encoder-decoder that requires specialized kernels (float16 quant path). We need to pin the exact build. If they can't run the smaller 13B fallback, we may hit memory pressure on shared nodes.
- Runtime compatibility: the dedicated pool in us-west is on runtime v1.24; the model's optimized kernels prefer v1.27. We can backport the kernel patches but that is a 24–36 hour ops effort.
- KV cache & multi-req batching: their traffic shape shows long context and reuse — we can enable aggressive KV caching which reduces GPU time but increases RAM pressure on the host. Need Ops to validate host memory headroom.

What I can offer for the 72-hour window if we move fast:
1) Standby lane of 4 GPUs on day 1 (validate kernel compatibility on one canary slot).
2) If Atlas is willing to pin to a 13B variant for the first 24 hours, we can provision +3 GPUs (total 7) while we complete the runtime patch.
3) If Runtime patch completed on day 2, we can expand to 10 GPUs but only under a strict autoscale gating mechanism and with documented rollback thresholds (OOM rate > 1% OR latency 99p > 2s).

I will draft a minimal ops-runbook and attach it to this thread. Ops will require a scheduled on-call signoff and a test canary (30 minutes at medium QPS) before full expansion.

-Marcus
Principal Infra Engineer — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: ops-runbook-draft.md

From: Mike Chen <mike@atlasai.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, Jul 20, 2026 at 09:03 AM -07:00
Subject: Re: Emergency slate carve-in & short-notice autoscale exception for Atlas.ai pilot

All —

Thanks for the rapid read. We can be flexible on a few items:
- Model pinning: we can run a 13B fallback for the first 24 hours. Our production 70B runs tend to kick in on day 2 of a multi-day test, so that aligns with your suggested ramp.
- Start window: we can shift the start by +6 hours to accommodate kernel backport testing.
- Minimum guaranteed: we can accept 6 GPUs as a minimum for the first 24 hours, then ramp to 10 if kernels validated. Peak concurrent slots — 14 tokens-heavy requests at peak (approx).

We will sign the MOU and cover incremental GPU hours — legal is ready. If you need a short written confirmation, I can send it within 2 hours.

-Mike
Head of Partnerships, Atlas.ai

Team —

Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround. Recap & decisions: 
- Grant standby lane of 4 GPUs for 2026-07-22 15:00 PT -> 2026-07-25 15:00 PT (shifted +6h as requested).
- Conditional expansion path: +3 GPUs (to 7) if Atlas runs 13B fallback for first 24h. Full 10 GPUs only after runtime patch validated (expected day 2) and on-call signoff.
- Autoscale exception: temporary cap to 10 concurrent slots allowed with Ops gating (on-call signoff + canary validation).
- Finance: Atlas will sign MOU and pay for incremental hours; Laura to coordinate billing/credits language.
- Next steps: Marcus to post ops-runbook (attach ops-runbook-draft.md) and schedule a 30-minute canary at low QPS before full ramp. Dev to coordinate moving noncritical evals to preemptible nodes to free up resources. Kimberly to prepare a one-paragraph customer note in case of SLA knock-on.

Mike — please send the MOU confirmation when you have it. I will file a quick Jira (INFRA-3427) and add the runbook & attachments to the Drive folder.

Thanks — pulling this together fast was great.
Irene
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
